237: 
238:     # If we have no boundaries, we get no score.
239:     if len(reference_boundaries) == 0 or len(estimated_boundaries) == 0:
240:         return 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
241: 
242:     matching = util.match_events(reference_boundaries, estimated_boundaries, window)
243: 
244:     precision = float(len(matching)) / len(estimated_boundaries)
245:     recall = float(len(matching)) / len(reference_boundaries)
246: 
247:     f_measure = util.f_measure(precision, recall, beta=beta)
248: 
249:     return precision, recall, f_measure
250: 
251: 
252: def deviation(reference_intervals, estimated_intervals, trim=False):
253:     """Compute the median deviations between reference
254:     and estimated boundary times.
255: 
256:     Examples
257:     --------
258:     >>> ref_intervals, _ = mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals('ref.lab')
259:     >>> est_intervals, _ = mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals('est.lab')
260:     >>> r_to_e, e_to_r = mir_eval.boundary.deviation(ref_intervals,
261:     ...                                              est_intervals)
262: 
263:     Parameters
264:     ----------
265:     reference_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n, 2)
266:         reference segment intervals, in the format returned by
267:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_intervals` or
268:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
269:     estimated_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(m, 2)
270:         estimated segment intervals, in the format returned by
271:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_intervals` or
272:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
273:     trim : boolean
274:         if ``True``, the first and last intervals are ignored.
275:         Typically, these denote start (0.0) and end-of-track markers.
276:         (Default value = False)
277: 
278:     Returns
279:     -------
280:     reference_to_estimated : float
281:         median time from each reference boundary to the
282:         closest estimated boundary
283:     estimated_to_reference : float
284:         median time from each estimated boundary to the
285:         closest reference boundary
286:     """
287:     validate_boundary(reference_intervals, estimated_intervals, trim)
288: 
289:     # Convert intervals to boundaries
290:     reference_boundaries = util.intervals_to_boundaries(reference_intervals)
291:     estimated_boundaries = util.intervals_to_boundaries(estimated_intervals)
292: 
293:     # Suppress the first and last intervals
294:     if trim:
295:         reference_boundaries = reference_boundaries[1:-1]
296:         estimated_boundaries = estimated_boundaries[1:-1]
297: 
298:     # If we have no boundaries, we get no score.
299:     if len(reference_boundaries) == 0 or len(estimated_boundaries) == 0:
300:         return np.nan, np.nan
301: 
302:     dist = np.abs(np.subtract.outer(reference_boundaries, estimated_boundaries))
303: 
304:     estimated_to_reference = np.median(dist.min(axis=0))
305:     reference_to_estimated = np.median(dist.min(axis=1))
306: 
307:     return reference_to_estimated, estimated_to_reference
308: 
309: 
310: def pairwise(
311:     reference_intervals,
312:     reference_labels,
313:     estimated_intervals,
314:     estimated_labels,
315:     frame_size=0.1,
316:     beta=1.0,
317: ):
318:     """Frame-clustering segmentation evaluation by pair-wise agreement.
319: 
320:     Examples
321:     --------
322:     >>> (ref_intervals,
323:     ...  ref_labels) = mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals('ref.lab')
324:     >>> (est_intervals,
325:     ...  est_labels) = mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals('est.lab')
326:     >>> # Trim or pad the estimate to match reference timing
327:     >>> (ref_intervals,
328:     ...  ref_labels) = mir_eval.util.adjust_intervals(ref_intervals,
329:     ...                                               ref_labels,
330:     ...                                               t_min=0)
331:     >>> (est_intervals,
332:     ...  est_labels) = mir_eval.util.adjust_intervals(
333:     ...     est_intervals, est_labels, t_min=0, t_max=ref_intervals.max())
334:     >>> precision, recall, f = mir_eval.structure.pairwise(ref_intervals,
335:     ...                                                    ref_labels,
336:     ...                                                    est_intervals,
337:     ...                                                    est_labels)
338: 
339:     Parameters
340:     ----------
341:     reference_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(n, 2)
342:         reference segment intervals, in the format returned by
343:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
344:     reference_labels : list, shape=(n,)
345:         reference segment labels, in the format returned by
346:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
347:     estimated_intervals : np.ndarray, shape=(m, 2)
348:         estimated segment intervals, in the format returned by
349:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
350:     estimated_labels : list, shape=(m,)
351:         estimated segment labels, in the format returned by
352:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_labeled_intervals`.
353:     frame_size : float > 0
354:         length (in seconds) of frames for clustering
355:         (Default value = 0.1)
356:     beta : float > 0
357:         beta value for F-measure
358:         (Default value = 1.0)
359: 
360:     Returns
361:     -------
362:     precision : float > 0
363:         Precision of detecting whether frames belong in the same cluster
364:     recall : float > 0
365:         Recall of detecting whether frames belong in the same cluster
366:     f : float > 0
367:         F-measure of detecting whether frames belong in the same cluster
368: 
369:     """
370:     validate_structure(
371:         reference_intervals, reference_labels, estimated_intervals, estimated_labels
372:     )
373: 
374:     # Check for empty annotations.  Don't need to check labels because
375:     # validate_structure makes sure they're the same size as intervals
376:     if reference_intervals.size == 0 or estimated_intervals.size == 0:
377:         return 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
378: 
379:     # Generate the cluster labels
380:     y_ref = util.intervals_to_samples(
381:         reference_intervals, reference_labels, sample_size=frame_size
382:     )[-1]
383: 
384:     y_ref = util.index_labels(y_ref)[0]
385: 
386:     # Map to index space
387:     y_est = util.intervals_to_samples(
388:         estimated_intervals, estimated_labels, sample_size=frame_size
389:     )[-1]
390: 
391:     y_est = util.index_labels(y_est)[0]
392:
